rules_text:
Rules summary 5 Corgis with all different numbers = 1 point 5 Corgis with all the same number = 2 points 5 Corgis with all the same color = 2 points You also get +1 bonus point if all 5 cards in the set have the same type of fur (fawn/tan/gold, or black fuyr). First to score of 5 wins! You are trying to fill your 3 available kennels to score the above points. On your turn you will draw at least 2, and up to 4, hoping not to reveal 2 with the same number (if you do, you are forced to give everything you drew to another player) Be careful, if you do not have a place in one of your kennels for all the cards, you will have to choose one kennel, and discard all cards in it. Then you can place the remaining cards in the (now empty) kennel. Special/event cards (when drawn, resolve the event immediately. They are not counted towards your minimum 2 draws that turn. - Baseball: All players take a card from the top of the deck, and immediately place into their kennels. - Bones: You may choose a (non-wild) Corgi card from the discard pile, and immediately add it to your kennels. - Collar: You are forced to draw 2 more cards from the deck. - Bowl: Take a peek at the top card of the deck, and decide whether to stop drawing cards immediately. - Fleas: Immediately steal a visible card from an opponent's kennel and place it in one of your kennels.

---

Are you ready to play the shortest, furriest, and most adorable card game? Dive into Crazy Corgi and scramble to find a kennel for your fluffy puppies. Get too greedy, though, and the corgis will dash to another player!

Crazy Corgi is a game for 2-4 players, ages 6 and up. The goal is to score points by placing cards in your three "kennels", creating sets of five cards that are worth different points depending on the combinations.

At the beginning of each turn, you draw 2-4 cards from the deck, hoping not to reveal two with the same number. If you succeed, you add those cards to your kennels; otherwise, the cards are given to another player, who will place them in their kennels. However, if you can't add a card to a kennel without creating an invalid combination, you must discard one of your kennels to start a new one. The player who scores 5 points first wins.

—description from the publisher

[Rating: 1/10] Almost a Knizia style game like No Mercy or Circus Flohcati. But.... it felt a little too generous, like there's rarely a bad move since it's so easy to get a set to work out somehow. And then the interaction to mess up someone else's set takes too much brainpower, so it stops feeling like a silly party game, and more a game about perfect calculation.

[Rating: 2/10] Incredibly random with no discernible choices to make. It was so bad I honestly thought we had the rules wrong.

[Rating: 3/10] The artwork is great, but personally theres not much to do for mee in this game. You bust to quickly, you make some 'random' sets to score minimal points. I hope Im missing something.
